question: Explain the meaning of 'previous year' under the Income-tax Act, 1961. In which cases is the income of a previous year taxed in that previous year itself?

points.label: Meaning
points.description: The previous year is the financial year immediately before the assessment year; for a newly set up business or profession, or a new source of income, it runs from the date of setting up or the date the source arises to the end of that financial year.

points.label: General rule and why exceptions exist
points.description: Normally income of a previous year is taxed in the next (assessment) year; exceptions exist where waiting could lead to loss of revenue.

points.label: Shipping business of non-residents
points.description: Income of a non-resident from carrying passengers, goods or mail from a port in India is taxed on each voyage before the ship leaves.

points.label: Persons leaving India
points.description: Where an individual is likely to leave India during the year with no present intention of returning, income up to the date of departure can be assessed in the same year.

points.label: AOP or BOI for a particular event
points.description: An association of persons, body of individuals or artificial juridical person formed for a particular event or purpose that is likely to be dissolved can be assessed in the same year.

points.label: Transfer to avoid tax and discontinued business
points.description: Persons likely to transfer their assets to avoid tax, and businesses or professions that are discontinued, may also be assessed in the same year.
